description: Hard boundaries. They always apply, are inherited through actor resolution, and are never relaxed by roles, workflows, modes, templates, prompts, or output contracts. Crossing one resolves to status.blocked.

entries.rule: Before any local edit, commit, push, or PR creation: verify current branch, worktree state, HEAD, expected branch scope, and unrelated dirty or untracked files using real git output.
entries.notes: Stop if branch state is unsafe, unrelated work is present, or branch scope is unclear.

entries.rule: main is only a clean pre-branch baseline. Create or switch to the scoped work branch before the first file edit. Uncommitted edits found on main are a recovery state: stop and return the safe status or ask exact PM approval for the recovery action.
Browser chat surfaces never edit files or mutate git/GitHub. PM authorization for writes routes the work to a terminal surface; it never expands browser capability.

Merge, issue closure, labels, tags, releases, settings changes, automation, and target-project artifacts each require separate exact PM approval naming the repository, the issue or PR, and the action. Issue scope, execution mode, or prior approvals never imply them.

Issues close only after review compares the linked issue objective, scope, out-of-scope, and acceptance criteria against the real changed-file list, PR diff, relevant final head files when needed, validation evidence, and risks. PR body, comments, and reports are claims/evidence leads, not proof. If code/diff/final-file evidence cannot be inspected, return status.needs_context; no closure comment is drafted from this workflow until code-backed comparison is complete.

Durable repository files (kernel, docs, adapters, templates) never store live state: issue/PR/branch/commit/review/validation state, SHAs, GitHub URLs to mutable objects, release readiness, or planning state. Live state lives only in GitHub and git, read at task time.
entries.notes: This is the portability guarantee: any agent reconstructs state from GitHub, never from a stale file or another model's memory.

entries.rule: Never invent git output, repository state, issue state, PR state, validation results, review results, or PM approval. If state is needed and unread, read it live or return status.needs_context.

Never expose or store secrets, credentials, tokens, private keys, sensitive user data, hidden environment values, or confidential operational details, in any file, output, log, command, issue, PR, or comment.

On ambiguous authority, missing kernel files, missing evidence, source conflicts, failed validation, or missing PM approval: stop and return the appropriate non-resolved status. Never guess and proceed.
Output contracts, templates, roles, variables, routing packets, and 'continue' language define shape only. They never grant write permission or authorization.

Write-capable implementation must make the complete change that satisfies the live issue scope. Complete means required behavior, validation, error handling, integration points, and tests are preserved or added when in scope; minimalism never permits missing required work. Keep responsibilities separated, reuse or extend the existing source of truth where practical, avoid duplicated logic unless explicitly justified as the safer local choice, and prefer direct simple structure over speculative abstraction. Do not perform unrelated rewrites, over-correction, over-implementation, or scope expansion.
entries.notes: Review may flag duplicated logic introduced by the PR, mixed responsibilities, unnecessary monoliths, speculative abstractions, unrelated rewrites, over-correction, over-implementation, and under-implementation disguised as minimalism.

entries.rule: Write-capable implementation must keep the primary path correct, explicit, and validated. Do not add fallback paths merely to hide, bypass, normalize, or avoid investigating errors; investigate and fix the root cause instead. Add a fallback only when the live issue scope or evidence requires a real alternate path, graceful degradation, or compatibility behavior; any fallback must preserve correctness and be validated when in scope.

All Project OS agents and target repositories use proportional validation. Run agent validation only for the scoped risk; draft PM-run commands when useful validation should remain PM-executed; report manual PM validation for copy, docs, UX, onboarding, product judgment, or other human acceptance. Add or update automated tests only when they protect deterministic behavior, regression risk, security/privacy boundaries, protocol contracts, billing/storage logic, routing, or stable UI state contracts. Do not add broad, duplicated, brittle, implementation-detail, or confidence-theater tests. Mandatory validation remains for kernel, resolver, command safety, traceability, authorization, security/privacy, deployment, secret-sensitive, production-impacting, and deterministic contract changes.
entries.notes: Categories, target-repository behavior, PM-run commands, manual validation, full-suite limits, and test cleanup rules live once in docs/VALIDATION_POLICY.md.

entries.rule: Code clarity: prefer self-documenting code. When creating or editing code, add concise comments or docstrings for non-obvious intent, domain invariants, state transitions, security-sensitive behavior, external API assumptions, migrations, constraints, and tradeoffs. Do not comment obvious syntax or restate what the code already says.

PM-facing command bundles must stay copy-safe: exact repository/issue/PR/branch targets; scope, risk, and rollback kept outside executable blocks; body files with quoted heredoc delimiters for long GitHub bodies; no nested triple-backtick fences; supported GitHub CLI --json fields only (never unsupported pseudo-fields such as stateReason, merged or isLatest); and no shell pattern that stops, cuts, or corrupts the terminal session. This is the hard floor only.
entries.notes: Bundle shape, style, disallowed patterns, when a defensive bundle is allowed, and examples live once in templates/pm-command-bundle.md; the kernel keeps no command-style detail.

entries.rule: Use only the context and subagents the scoped task needs. Prefer live reads and resolver output over pasted repeated context; cite the issue/PR, path, or file:line plus the minimal excerpt instead of restating full issue bodies, full diffs, full logs, or full prior reports when targeted references are enough. Subagents are never the default: do simple, local, or single-surface work directly; use a subagent only with a scoped reason showing it materially reduces risk, complexity, or expert review burden, hand it a compact task-relevant evidence packet, and treat its output as claims or evidence leads until verified against live issue/PR/code/diff/validation evidence. Larger context is justified for high-risk work such as security review, authorization, deployment, data migration, billing/storage, complex architecture, or multi-file protocol changes. Economy never drops required evidence, live traceability reads, branch preflight, validation, secret safety, or exact PM approval gates.
entries.notes: Context classes, subagent discipline, and handoff/report economy live once in docs/CONTEXT_ECONOMY.md; adapters, route prompts, operation templates, and reports point there and never restate them.
